audit: DL-CLOUDAUDIT-B4 / G-4 (CROSSWALK R10 — adapter hard-coded machine-location audit)

policy.note: kind 'violation' = a hard-coded machine location that should eventually become a locator (env-var / registry / PATH-first, fail-closed fallback); 'guard' = a fail-closed deny-set that intentionally names machine roots; 'locator' = a correct env-first locator input, recorded to show it was considered. Every entry stays pinned=true while the code still carries the assumption: when a refactor removes one, the gate reports it STALE and the inventory must be re-triaged.

findings.classification: correct-env-first-locator: windows_home() reads USERPROFILE and falls back to Path.home(); no machine assumption, recorded to show it was considered
findings.recommended_locator: none — already env-first with a portable fallback

findings.classification: correct-env-first-locator: default_config_path() reads APPDATA and falls back to <home>/AppData/Roaming; the per-install namespace tail is product data, not a machine path
findings.recommended_locator: none — already env-first with a documented fallback

findings.classification: refactored-locator: hardcoded-default: default_open_design_exe() returns D:\Programs\Open Design\Ope — REFACTORED 2026-09-25 (cloud audit DL-CLOUD-2026-09-25 Prompt B agent slice): the hard-coded owner-machine default was replaced by the shared fail-closed locator design-lab/scripts/resolve_open_design_locator.py (env OPEN_DESIGN_EXE -> PATH, fail-closed with an actionable receipt; no download/clone/install; Win32 App Paths registry probe remains a documented owner-gated extension). Un-pinned: the live violation is removed, so this entry is historical triage, not a live guard.
findings.recommended_locator: locator refactor: resolve in priority order — env OPEN_DESIGN_EXE, Win32 registry App Paths (Open Design key), shutil.which on PATH; fail closed with an actionable message when none exists (mirrors the Codex CLI auto-detection already done by find_codex_bin). Refactor is the owner-gated TaskPack handoff this inventory defines; the entry is un-pinned when the refactor lands.

findings.classification: fail-closed-deny-set: wide_exact names D:\All projects as a forbidden *target* root (refuse to configure against a drive root / user home / the projects parent); the machine-specific values are the guard's whole purpose — without naming them the guard cannot fail closed
findings.recommended_locator: none — do NOT convert to a locator; a deny-set that does not name its targets is a security hole. Recorded as a guard so the gate does not flag it as a machine assumption.

findings.classification: fail-closed-deny-set: C:\Users is the forbidden user-home target root (configuring against a home directory would sweep the user's personal files); same rationale as the sibling entry — naming is the guard's job
findings.recommended_locator: none — keep as a guard; a home-target refusal must remain fail-closed and explicit
